source.title: Rethinking Associative Memory Mechanism in Induction Head

page_placements.theme: ICL transience and competition with in-weights learning

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The paper is dated July 9, 2025 despite the supplied year being 2024; no missing text is inferred.
record.tranche_reason: It tests induction-pattern behavior and previous-token attention in trained two-layer transformers, but uses a triggered-bigram setup, positional-encoding comparisons, and memory-recall and prediction measures rather than the original phase-change measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper tests previous-token associations, next-token predictions from repeated patterns, and sensitivity to positional encoding and sequence length. It does not test abrupt formation alongside an in-context-learning loss gain or bump, large-transformer coverage, or few-shot task learning. Theoretical constructions and cited results are not recorded as empirical rows; Fig. 3's qualitative attention patterns are recorded separately from the numerical attention scores in Table 2.
record.test_reason: The study trains small two-layer transformers on triggered-bigram data. It measures how well the first-layer previous-token head forms, using memory recall, attention score and attention maps. It also measures induction-style completion ([A][B]…[A]→[B]) accuracy and compares absolute (APE) with relative (RPE) positional encoding. These results bear on the induction mechanism (V1) and on its dependence on the training setup (V5). It does not use the original phase-change or loss-curve method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that RPE lets a two-layer transformer capture in-context patterns across longer sequences, whereas APE's previous-token head fails at later positions. They add that next-token output balances in-context pattern frequency against global bigram knowledge. They caution that the results may not generalize to LLMs and that induction heads explain only part of ICL.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments train two-layer toy transformers on triggered-bigram data and compare APE with RPE using memory recall, attention scores, and prompted next-token predictions. They do not reproduce the original training phase-change and loss-curve analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior changes with positional encoding (APE versus RPE), sequence length and the train/evaluation length mismatch, and the relative frequency of repeated patterns in the prompt.

fits_no_version.finding: Next-token output reflects competition between in-context pattern frequency and pretrained bigram knowledge. Global-knowledge predictions are more likely when B1 and B2 counts are equal or near maximum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-head outputs are modulated by, and can be overridden by, pretrained global (bigram) knowledge.

record.problems: The experiments use two-layer transformers and controlled synthetic or constructed data; the authors caution that results may not generalize to LLMs. Several attention-pattern and prediction results are reported only in figures. No direct causal test isolates the composition of the previous-token and induction heads.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Theoretical constructions and cited findings were not entered as empirical results.

untested.parts: No causal test (ablation or patching) of composition between the previous-token head and the induction head; composition is inferred from theory and attention measures.
Only positional encoding and train/eval length are varied. Data properties and persistence of in-context learning are not tested.
Not tested: Fig. 1a shows a memory-recall training trajectory but the timing of formation is not analysed.
Not tested; the authors only say in the Limitations that ICL uses other circuits too.

missing.what: Fig. 1a includes an APE memory-recall curve restricted to t<128 (wk1_(t<128)_acc), which separates within-range from out-of-range recall.
The RPE first-layer head sometimes attends to the current token rather than the previous one (qualitative).

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 'score' columns are labelled attention scores in the caption but described alongside memory recall in the text; the attention-score reading is kept. Theoretical results (Theorems 1–3, Propositions 1–3) are not used as rows. The 'recall' and 'score' measures read the previous-token association directly; the induction head itself is evaluated only through prediction accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not causally isolate composition between the previous-token head and the induction head; its experiments measure previous-token associations and prediction behavior.
No test of abrupt formation, a narrow training window, a contemporaneous in-context-learning gain, or a training-loss bump.
No measurement of most in-context learning in large transformers or of loss changes across token indices.
No sweep across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
The study tests positional encoding and sequence-length settings in its two-layer setup, but not a broad range of data properties or whether in-context learning persists across training setups.
No experiment compares induction heads with other mechanisms on few-shot task learning.
No analysis of whether formation consists of multiple sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

relationships.reason: RPE stores over 90% of previous-token associations and keeps previous-token attention (0.95/0.93). It completes repeated patterns accurately (0.87–0.90), and its predictions track in-context pattern frequency (R1, R7–R10, R12, R13).
relationships.display_finding: Relative positional encoding stored over 90% of previous-token associations, maintained previous-token attention of 0.95/0.93, and achieved completion accuracy of 0.87–0.90, with predictions tracking pattern frequency.

relationships.condition: APE two-layer transformers, later positions or longer sequences
relationships.reason: Under APE the previous-token head fails beyond t≈100–128. Attention score falls to 0.198 and accuracy drops to 0.79, so the mechanism is position-limited (R2, R4, R5, R6, R11).
relationships.display_finding: Previous-token attention failed beyond positions approximately 100–128, with attention falling to 0.198 and completion accuracy to 0.79.
